title: Age Calculator: How to Calculate Your Exact Age in Years, Months and Days
seo: Age Calculator — Exact Age in Years, Months & Days
meta: Calculate your exact age in years, months and days for job forms, exams and ID applications. Worked examples, cut-off dates and common mistakes explained.
body:
Why "just subtract the years" gets your age wrong

Most people work out their age by subtracting their birth year from the current year. That only works if your birthday has already happened this year. If it has not, you are a year younger than that subtraction says — and on a job form, exam application or ID document, one year can be the difference between eligible and rejected.

Exact age has three parts: completed years, then completed months since your last birthday, then remaining days. That is the format most forms expect, and it is what the free Age Calculator on this site produces from just two dates: your date of birth and the date you want your age on.

How to calculate exact age, step by step

Step 1 — Completed years. Subtract your birth year from the target year. Then subtract one more year if your birthday has not happened yet in the target year.

Step 2 — Completed months. Count whole months from your last birthday to the target date. If the target day-of-month is before your birth day-of-month, you have not completed that month yet, so count one month less.

Step 3 — Remaining days. Count the days from your last completed month anniversary to the target date. This is where month lengths matter: a "month" is not 30 days, it is a calendar month, so February and 31-day months give different day counts.

Try it with the Age Calculator above: enter your date of birth, leave "age on" as today (or set the form's cut-off date), and it does all three steps for you. Nothing is uploaded — the calculation runs in your browser.

Worked example 1: birthday already passed this year

Date of birth: 12 March 2001. Target date: 5 November 2026.

Completed years: 2026 − 2001 = 25, and the birthday (12 March) has passed, so it stays 25. Completed months from 12 March to 5 November: March→October is 7 full months, plus the days from 12 October to 5 November, which is 24 days. Exact age: 25 years, 7 months, 24 days.

Worked example 2: birthday still to come

Date of birth: 20 December 1998. Target date: 5 November 2026.

Naive subtraction gives 2026 − 1998 = 28, but the birthday has not happened yet, so completed years are 27. From the last birthday (20 December 2025) to 5 November 2026 is 10 completed months plus 16 days. Exact age: 27 years, 10 months, 16 days — a full year less than the naive answer.

Worked example 3: the leap-year trap

Date of birth: 29 February 2004. In a non-leap year there is no 29 February, so most systems treat the birthday as 28 February or 1 March depending on the form's rules — check the form, do not guess. Age on 5 November 2026 is still 22 completed years (birthday treated as passed), 8 months and a few days, either way. The year count does not change; only the day count shifts by one.

Age on a cut-off date, not today

Government jobs, exams and admissions almost never ask "how old are you today". They ask your age on a specific date — for example, 1 January 2027 or the last date for applications. Always use that cut-off date in the calculator, not today's date. A candidate who is 28 today may be 29 on the cut-off date, or still 27 — and the form will be judged on the cut-off date.

Common cut-off mistakes: using the application date instead of the notified cut-off date, counting the birth year as year one (that gives an age one year too high), and rounding months up to the next month.

Age in total days, weeks and months

Some forms and medical records ask for total days lived or total months. Once you have the exact date difference, those are simple conversions: total days is the calendar difference between the two dates (the calculator's year/month/day breakdown already accounts for leap years), total months is completed years × 12 plus completed months, and total weeks is total days ÷ 7 rounded down. Do not multiply years by 365 — leap years make that answer wrong by roughly one day per four years.

FAQ

Is my age 25 or 26 if my birthday is tomorrow? You are still 25 until the birthday itself. Age changes on the birthday, not the day before.

Why do two calculators give different day counts? Usually one counts the start date and the other does not, or one treats a month as 30 days. The calendar method used here — completed years, then months, then days — matches how official forms read age.

What date should I use for an ID or passport form? The date of birth exactly as printed on your birth certificate or existing ID, even if your family remembers a different date. Mismatched dates cause more rejections than wrong arithmetic.

Does the calculator store my date of birth? No. It runs locally in your browser and nothing is sent to a server.

Checklist before you submit a form

1. Use the form's cut-off date, not today. 2. Copy the date of birth exactly from your official document. 3. Check whether your birthday has passed in the target year. 4. If you were born on 29 February, confirm how that form treats it. 5. Keep the years/months/days breakdown, not just the year count.
